detail:
NIAMS describes fibromyalgia as a long-lasting disorder that causes pain and tenderness throughout the body, along with fatigue and trouble sleeping. Scientists do not fully understand its cause, but people with the disorder have an increased sensitivity to pain: brain imaging studies and other research have found altered signaling in the neural pathways that transmit and receive pain.

Mayo Clinic describes the current diagnostic approach, based on American College of Rheumatology criteria: widespread pain lasting at least 3 months, with pain in at least 4 of 5 body regions, and no other condition that explains it; the older tender-point examination is no longer required. Because fibromyalgia is not a form of arthritis and does not inflame or damage tissue, normal scans and labs are common, and evaluation focuses on the symptom pattern and on excluding other causes.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for widespread pain.
summary: NIAMS describes fibromyalgia as a chronic disorder of widespread pain and tenderness with fatigue and sleep problems, in which the nervous system appears to amplify pain signals; it does not damage joints or muscles.
takeaways: pain sensitivity is increased, not caused by joint damage
diagnosis uses symptom criteria, not a single lab test
fatigue, sleep, and thinking problems travel with the pain
ask your doctor to rule out look-alike conditions
title: Fibromyalgia: widespread pain and heightened sensitivity
